On Monday, while walking to the corner shop, I had to stop recording a voicenote because I was being pummelled by small yet insistent hailstones. On Tuesday, I squelched to the station amid a downpour, rain seeping into my shoes. Today, I’m slipping a tube of factor 50 into my bag and googling which local cafes have the best aircon. Temperatures are predicted to hit 28C in London, beating the 26.6C previously recorded at Kew Gardens on 8 April to make it the hottest day of the year so far.

In a week of weather whiplash, people up and down the UK have been left slightly shellshocked by this sudden, drastic change – so what’s going on? Why did we seem to start off in winter and transition to summer overnight?

It’s all about airstreams, otherwise known as wind direction, and where they’re coming from, according to Jim Dale, senior meteorologist at British Weather Services.

“What happened at the beginning of May is that we inherited a modified polar airstream,” he says. “The polar front came down – that’s the division between temperate air. What that meant was we were in a cool-to-cold block rather than anything warm, and we’ve remained in it for most of the month.”

What’s caused the swift change now is almost the reversal of that process: “The polar front is going further north, and that allows in the southerly airflow of Africa across Spain, across France into the UK – and hey presto, air pressure rises and we get the sunshine and the warmer temperatures, and with it the humidity, and probably the odd thunderstorm.”

Jason Nicholls, lead international forecaster for AccuWeather, adds that the reason for the big change heading into the weekend is the ridge of high pressure near Spain building over western Europe over the next few days. “The building ridge will lift the jet stream and storm track north of the UK, which was aimed at northern Europe, leading to the cool and wet weather over the last several days,” he says. “The peak of the warmth in the UK is expected this weekend into early next week.”

A heatwave is expected across the UK over the bank holiday weekend ( PA )

This weekend, temperatures could hit 30C in parts of the South East. If that happens before bank holiday Monday, it will be the earliest date this has happened in the UK for more than 70 years.

Yellow heat health alerts, aimed at those who are particularly vulnerable, such as the elderly and those with existing health conditions, have been issued by the Met Office for five English regions: the East Midlands, the East of England, London, the West Midlands and the South East. They come into force at 9am on Friday and will remain in place until 5pm on Tuesday 27 May.

The warm weather is likely to meet the criteria for a heatwave, defined by the Met Office as a minimum of three consecutive days of daily maximum temperatures exceeding a county-specific threshold. In London, that temperature is set at 28C, whereas in cooler parts of the UK, such as Northern Ireland, it’s 25C.

“It looks like this one that we’re going into has got legs,” says Dale of the latest warm-weather stint. “In other words, it’s not just going to be two days, three days, and then back out again. I think this may well last for some time.”

Wild swings in the weather pattern in spring are par for the course Jason Nicholls, AccuWeather

The other good news – for sunbathers, if not gardeners – is that we’re unlikely to experience a soggy transition from May to June. “I don’t think we’ll see particularly high levels of rainfall now, if at all before the end of the month,” predicts Dale.

And although it may feel like an unusually dramatic shift in weather, there’s no cause for concern; it’s to be expected at this time of year, say the experts. “These pattern changes are common, especially in the transitional seasons of spring and autumn,” explains Nicholls, citing a similar swing in May last year; the high on 5 May 2025 was 13C, and on 11 May jumped to 26C. “May 2024 also had such a pattern change, so wild swings in the weather pattern in spring are par for the course in the mid-latitudes,” he adds.

Spring typically delivers what Dale describes as “very Jekyll and Hyde weather”: “That’s the very nature of spring – it has several faces. It’s not that unusual to go from a very warm to a cold spell or vice versa.”

It’s all just a matter of perspective, really. So relax, enjoy – and maybe keep an umbrella on standby next to the factor 50, just in case.

Scientists have discovered a new marine dinosaur species that grew 43ft and terrorised the seas over 80 million years ago.

Tylosaurus rex – T rex for short – was a massive mosasaur reptile that lived primarily in what is now northern Texas.

Its name means “king of the tylosaurs”, researchers say, distinguishing it from the iconic land dinosaur Tyrannosaurus rex, which translates to “tyrant lizard”.

“Besides being huge, roughly twice the length of the largest great white sharks, T rex appeared to be a much meaner animal than other mosasaurs,” said Ron Tykoski, author of a new study published in the journal Bulletin of the American Museum of Natural History.

“Through our study and examination of well-preserved fossils collected throughout the north Texas region, we have evidence of violence within this species to a degree not previously seen in other Tylosaurus specimens.”

open image in gallery T rex ( Perot Museum of Nature and Science )

Researchers analysed fossils kept at the American Museum of Natural History as well as more than a dozen similar samples held at other institutions, following suspicion that they represented a different animal.

These fossils had finely serrated teeth, a trait uncommon among mosasaurs.

They were also four million years younger than the species Tylosaurus proriger to which the specimen were thought to belong.

open image in gallery Tylosaurus rex holotype skeleton ( Perot Museum of Nature and Science )

Researchers arrived at the name T rex in homage to the palaeontologist John Thurmond, who first recognised tylosaurs as a new species in the late 1960s.

The species had exceptionally strong jaw and neck muscles, suggesting that it was a powerful predator.

One T rex specimen housed in the Perot Museum’s collection, nicknamed “The Black Knight”, is missing the tip of the snout and has a fractured lower jaw, damage scientists claim could only be inflicted by its own species.

The findings suggest that relationships of known mosasaur species need to be re-examined, as most prior studies relied on the same, minimally modified dataset for decades.

open image in gallery Tylosaurus rex reconstruction ( Alderon Games )

Now, researchers have assembled a comprehensively revised mosasaur fossil sample dataset, which could lead to a new arrangement of evolutionary relationships among tylosaurs.

“It highlights the need to revisit long-standing assumptions about mosasaur evolution and to modernise the tools we use to study these iconic marine reptiles,” said Amelia Zietlow, a co-author of the study.

“These findings reshape both the physical and evolutionary picture of mosasaurs, underscoring Texas as a key region for understanding ancient marine ecosystems and signalling a new era of research into the evolutionary history of these formidable predators,” said Michael Polcyn, another study author,

News.title: Protesters storm Ebola hospital to retrieve victim’s body
News.content:
Protesters have stormed an Ebola treatment centre in the Democratic Republic of Congo to retrieve the body of a relative, according to local media reports.

Footage circulating online appeared to show parts of Rwampara Hospital engulfed in flames, with plumes of smoke rising above the facility. Gunshots can be heard in the background.

“Angry protesters are setting fire to the tents housing Ebola patients because they want to forcibly retrieve the bodies,” said one man, his face mask pulled below his mouth.

Health authorities oversee the burials of suspected victims in line with strict infection protocols, but this often brings them into conflict with grieving families who want to perform traditional burial rites for their loved ones.

Similar incidents have been a feature of previous Ebola outbreaks, particularly families digging up the bodies of deceased relatives for re-burial – an extremely dangerous act because corpses remain highly contagious for up to a week after death.

In 2022, a cluster of Ebola cases in Uganda was traced back to a family who exhumed their relative at night, undoing the work of a safe burial team in order to give the deceased man a funeral. Within days, at least 23 of the mourners had contracted Ebola and three were dead.

The unrest in Rwampara reportedly erupted on Thursday after the death of a young man suspected of having Ebola at the hospital, which is located around 7.5 miles from Bunia, the capital of the conflict-wracked eastern Ituri province.

News.title: Scientists to monitor British cruise passengers in hantavirus study
News.content:
British passengers repatriated from the cruise ship hit by an outbreak of hantavirus will be monitored for signs of infection as part of a long-term study.

More than 20 Britons who were potentially exposed to the disease on board the MV Hondius have volunteered for the study, which is being run by the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the University of Liverpool, the Pandemic Sciences Institute at the University of Oxford, the University of Edinburgh and the University of Glasgow.

It aims to generate robust research on the Andes strain of hantavirus, which is the only variant of the disease known to spread between people but is poorly understood and has no approved vaccine.

After they stop isolating, the volunteers will continue to provide blood samples for testing at Porton Down, the government research facility tasked with studying dangerous pathogens like Ebola, anthrax, and plague.

None of the British passengers who have returned to the UK have so far tested positive for hantavirus. But due to the virus’s long incubation period, which can be up to two months, it is possible they could still become unwell or be asymptomatic carriers of the disease.

One study has previously found that hantavirus could remain in human semen for up to six years and has the potential for sexual transmission, even after a person has recovered.

If a male patient tests positive for the virus, investigators will also look to test their semen for ongoing signs of infection.

“If we do have a case, we can study that in more detail and think about the mechanisms of the disease and how we can treat that disease better,” said Professor Lance Turtle, Chair in Immunity and Infectious Diseases at the University of Liverpool and Joint Chief Investigator in the study.

The Telegraph Fantasy Football season is now coming to a heated end. As always, the award-winning experts at Fantasy Football Hub continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

Telegraph Fantasy Football: last week's insights





Gunners Champions!

Arsenal have waited over two decades to be called league champions, and after another shut-out for Gabriel Magalhães (£4.5m) and company, and City’s draw at Bournemouth, Arteta’s men lifted the trophy. TFF managers may be worried about mass rotation for the Gunners in the final round of fixtures.

News.title: All-in-one chocolate cake
News.content:
Step

Spread the buttercream on one layer of cake – use a spatula or a palette knife – then put the other layer on top. Using a clean spatula or palette knife, spread the chocolate glaze on top of this layer (or drizzle it over) and encourage it down the sides of the cake. Neaten it all the way round with the palette knife. Leave to set a little before serving.

News.title: Welsh cakes
News.content: I’d never tasted a Welsh cake until I went to St Dogmaels local producers’ market for the BBC, some years back. I had them hot off the griddle with butter. They’re fragile and melting and much better than any scone. They’re also easy, quick to make and inexpensive, so just right for rainy-day weekend baking (when you bake a cake for someone else but want a treat for everyone in your house too), or even a midweek pick-me-up.

News.title: Lemon tart with blueberries
News.content:
The pastry here is from the California chef Lindsey Shere and it’s wonderful – thin and buttery and almost biscuity. You make it in a slightly different way, creaming the butter and sugar for it and then smearing it little by little with the heel of your hand (the French term is ‘fraisage’) once the flour has been added. There are good how-to videos online for the pastry method.

Do follow the chilling times and only add the amount of blueberries given here, otherwise they’ll bleed too much.

News.title: Flourless orange, almond and rosemary cake
News.content:
Step

Scrape the batter into the prepared tin and bake for 45 minutes, or until the cake is golden and you can feel that it is firm when you press the centre. The cake should also be coming away from the sides of the tin. Leave for 5 minutes, then unclasp the side and remove the surround from the cake, carefully peel the paper from the bottom and put it on to a plate.

Sports.title: Anyone who thinks this England squad can win World Cup needs their head tested – Tuchel has put his balls on the line
Sports.content:
THOMAS TUCHEL has properly put his b******s on the line with this England squad.

And the German is going to end up being hailed as a genius for the group of players he has selected – or a disaster.





Cole Palmer, Phil Foden, Harry Maguire, Morgan Gibbs-White, Adam Wharton and Levi Colwill are just some of the players missing.

And the big shock inclusion is Ivan Toney whose only appearance for Tuchel was as an 88th-minute sub against Senegal after he failed to impress in training at last summer’s post-season camp in Girona.

Individually, you can see why some of the players have missed out as the likes of Foden, in particular, do not deserve to be included.

But Maguire has been in good form for Manchester United and once he got a recall in March, he obviously thought he was back in.

England certainly need players of his experience which is why it is the right call to stick with Jordan Henderson.

Tuchel needs to be applauded for his bravery but this squad does not look particularly settled and I would still have also included Luke Shaw.

Also, Dan Burn is incredibly lucky to be in this squad and the same goes for Tino Livramento.

The defence looks bang-average and anyone who thinks this squad can win the World Cup needs to get their head tested.

Harry Kane yesterday claimed the squad has never been stronger but he is surely having a laugh.

And the fact England will still go into the tournament as one of the bookies’ favourites is a joke.

Tuchel called the players via phone between 4pm and 8pm to explain his decision while the official unveiling is at 10am tomorrow.

At 11am, he will talk to the media and his views will be intriguing.

Sports.title: Tottenham captain Cristian Romero ‘ditches relegation decider against Leeds to watch match 7000 miles away’
Sports.content:
CRISTIAN ROMERO will not be at Tottenham’s relegation decider on the final game of the Premier League season.

Spurs need just a point to survive in England’s top flight against Everton with West Ham two behind but with a much worse goal difference.





The Hammers face Leeds in Stratford while in North London, the Toffees will be looking to sink Roberto de Zerbi‘s side.

Romero, 28, will not be in the stands cheering on his team-mates despite being the club captain.

The Argentine will instead be attending a different football match 7,000MILES away.

Romero will instead be watching his boyhood club Belgrana take on River Plate in his homeland at the Estadio Monumental.

Belgrano are challenging for the Argentine Primera Division title despite having never won it in their history.

And opponents don’t come much more prestigious than River Plate.

His potential absence from the crucial game was revealed by South American football expert Tim Vickery.

Vickery said on talkSPORT: “He will be at the final of the Argentine Championship between Belgrano and River Plate.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“Belgrano are Romero’s club. It’s the club where he started, and he’s a fan.

“Belgrano have never won the Argentine Championship.

“They are going to River Plate, who have won more than anyone else, so this is historic.

“15 years ago, these two met in the play-off that relegated River Plate.



“If Tottenham going down is off the scale, River Plate going down is even more off the scale.”

Romero has not played since April after he picked up a knee injury in the 1-0 defeat at Sunderland.

In order for Tottenham to be relegated to the Championship, they will have to lose to Everton and West Ham will have to beat Leeds.

Spurs have only lost one of their last five games bu have only won twice at home this season in the league.

They will be desperate for a favour from former manager David Moyes at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Sports.title: After sexy Abbey Clancy ad recalls wild days of 2006 World Cup we ask were Wags REALLY to blame for England’s exit?
Sports.content:
SUITABLY well-oiled, the Wags arrived at Garibaldi’s bar in the sedate German spa town of Baden-Baden and ordered more champagne.

Some were soon dancing on tables amid shattered bubbly flutes as Coleen McLoughlin belted out an ode to her fiancé: “There’s Only One Wayne Rooney.”





Not to be outdone, Elen Rives serenaded the bar with a ditty for her then other half: “Super Frankie Lampard.”

Partying until 4am, and fuelled by bottles of Moet champagne drunk with strawberry syrup, glasses of vodka and Red Bull and shots of sambuca, the raucous party bellowed: “We’re not going home, we’re not going home.”

The bawdy singalong included a turn from the improbably named Neville Neville — father to defenders Phil and Gary — who attempted a rendition of God Save The Queen.

The players’ dad would later be pictured in newspapers clutching a replica World Cup, his exploits in the town appearing under a headline Neville Neville in Baden-Baden.



And striker Peter Crouch’s girlfriend Abbey Clancy, who this week stripped to a thong to promote a Wag-themed clothing collection for US brand Juicy Couture, would be sent home in disgrace after old pictures emerged of her snorting cocaine.

Meanwhile, a 20-minute drive into the Black Forest mountains at the secluded Schloss Buhlerhohe Hotel, the Wags’ husbands — England’s so-called Golden Generation of footballers — were trying to kick-start their stuttering 2006 World Cup campaign.

Two tortuous wins against Paraguay and Trinidad and Tobago and a heart-stopping draw against Sweden in the group stage hardly justified England’s position as second- favourites to win the tournament behind Brazil.

Ecuador awaited in the round of 16 knockout phase for a squad that included David Beckham, Steven Gerrard, Frank Lampard, Ashley Cole, Rio Ferdinand, John Terry, Wayne Rooney and Joe Cole.



And yet it was the wives and families who were stealing all the headlines with their exploits in what was starting to resemble a high-end hen do.

Then there was the shopping. Some of the group had spent £57,000 in one hour in designer clothes stores.

German tabloid Bild sneered: “They spend more in ten minutes than most of us do on our wardrobe in half a lifetime.”

And Spanish paper ABC trumpeted of the credit card spree: “Not even the stores of Vuitton and Gucci can keep up with the daily attack of the hooligans with Visas.”

It was the high watermark of Wag culture which featured in recent BBC documentary England 2006: The Golden Generation — and it is an era that Abbey Clancy, at least, is ready to resurrect. One skimpy T-shirt from the mum-of-four’s new range features the slogan “Juicy Wag”.



It’s quite a rehabilitation for the Wives And Girlfriends tag after Baden-Baden left them open to accusations that their behaviour had harmed the England team.

So did the Wags really derail the chance of glory for one of the most gifted Three Lions squads, or were they scapegoated after some shambolic performances on the pitch?

Then-manager Sven-Goran Eriksson had fought to base the team in Baden-Baden and for the Wags to be offered the chance to stay in the town.



Of the 23-man squad, only Aaron Lennon, 19, didn’t bring a partner. All invited family members, with the England entourage swelling to 110.

They were led by Victoria Beckham (dubbed Queen Wag) while Girls Aloud’s Cheryl Cole (then Tweedy), and Eriksson’s partner Nancy Dell’Olio also held court. For the Press, it was an irresistible mix of glamour and celebrity. There was the occasional football match too.

‘Isolated places’When Baden-Baden was unveiled as England’s base camp, Eriksson praised its “marvellous atmosphere, with some wonderful restaurants and cafes”.

They were ominous words — yet the FA believed the pretty town, with a population just over 55,000, was an ideal retreat for the squad and their families.

Then-FA chairman Brian Barwick recalled: “The (team) hotel and training base were miles out of town. We were up a hill and I thought it was one of the most isolated places I’d ever been to. We knew the players’ wives could stay down in the town in the Brenners Park Hotel and see their partners occasionally but generally be free to do what they wanted.”



The build-up to the tournament was dominated by Rooney’s race to be fit after breaking his fourth metatarsal in his right foot.

But after the first game — a cagey 1-0 win with a deflected own goal against Paraguay — the Wags took centre stage.

At the bar of their Brenners Park Hotel, peach bellinis in sugared champagne flutes were downed while Frederico’s resident pianist was being drowned out by a chorus of We Are The Champions. Pizzas and chips were served on silver platters followed by more peach bellinis, wine and beer.

While most of the group headed for bed around midnight.

But Coleen, Elen, Joe Cole’s now wife Carly Zucker, David Beckham’s sister Joanne and Steven Gerrard’s partner Alex Curran headed for Garibaldi’s — the restaurant and nightclub which would become Wags party central for three weeks.



Before the fun came to an end at 3am, the party downed £300-worth of Moet champagne and nine vodka Red Bulls, with Elen dancing on a bench in stilettos.

Baden-Baden’s Gucci and Hermes stores had bought in an extra £200,000 in stock, and much of it was snapped up by the Wags.

Bild newspaper wrote: “It has turned into Shopping-Shopping in Baden-Baden.”



A Fleet Street photographer described the women’s daily routine: “Morning coffee or maybe a run in town, shopping, back to the hotel, then on the p**s.

“It was full-on. They got no rest, so neither did we. Our rest days were when we got sent to cover the England matches.”

Initially reporting in other parts of Germany, after the Three Lions beat Ecuador to set up a quarter-final against Portugal, I too was drawn to Baden-Baden like a wasp to a plastic cup of stale lager.

Sun snapper Arthur Edwards and I made straight for hallowed Garibaldi’s and were rewarded with a front-page story as an extra 1,230 pints of lager were delivered for the thirsty England party.

Owner Carmine Tortora told us: “I’m delighted England beat Ecuador and hope they can stay in the competition as long as possible. I am Germany’s happiest bar owner.



“It’s been our best-ever two weeks of business.”

It didn’t take long to spot various Wags parading around the town.

I remember seeing a bewildered-looking Theo Walcott who Eriksson had brought along as a wild card despite not having started a Premier League game.

Then on July 1 England met Porttugal in Gelsenkirchen. Beckham was forced off with an Achilles injury early in the second half. In the 62nd minute, Rooney was sent off for stepping on Ricardo Carvalho.

Then Cristiano Ronaldo — Rooney’s Manchester United teammate — sprinted to the ref and demanded a red card.



Rooney went and the cameras caught Ronaldo winking at his bench. It was over.

Back in Baden-Baden there was time for a quick £30,000 shopping spree by the Wags and a last drink in Garibaldi’s.

Despite losing Beckham and Michael Owen to injury and Rooney admitting he had not recovered properly from his broken bone, some in the FA corridors of power blamed the Wags for World Cup failure.



Last year Gary Neville said on the Stick To Football podcast: “I can only describe it as an absolute circus. It wasn’t with the wives (that I was annoyed) but the whole organisation of the trip.

“There were stories breaking every day. ‘They’ve eaten here today,’ or ‘They’ve shopped here’ — it was just a constant distraction.

“When the players went to their press conferences, they were being asked about it all the time.”

Coleen said on the same podcast that reports of excessive partying were “exaggerated”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The mum-of-four added: “We couldn’t stay in a hotel all day — we had to go out and get food and enjoy ourselves.



“I do think it was unfair, the way we got called out for it, that we got the blame for having a good time.”

Sports.title: ‘Deplorable’ Southampton ‘pressured intern to spy on rivals in Tonda Eckert-backed plot’, EFL Spygate findings reveal
Sports.content:
“DEPLORABLE” Southampton LIED about recording opposition training sessions before boss Tonda Eckert admitted his key role in spying after evidence was uncovered.

The Saints are also guilty of putting pressure on junior staff members to spy on rivals.





The South Coast outfit are in meltdown after the FA launched its own investigation into the Spygate saga that has rocked the club – threatening even more savage punishments.

As Sun Sport exclusively revealed last week, Eckert could face a possible ban, potentially up to 18 months, along with any other figures responsible for the club’s spying missions. While his part in the whole operation leaves his position in serious doubt.

Southampton are already reeling after being sensationally booted out of the play-offs and hit with a four-point deduction for next season for spying on Middlesbrough, Ipswich and Oxford.

St Mary’s chiefs saw a desperate, last-gasp appeal rejected by an independent panel on Wednesday night, completely torching their dreams of a £215MILLION promotion jackpot.

But a fresh bombshell rocked the spying Saints as the EFL’s release of the written reasons as to why an independent commission expelled them revealed how they initially lied about the snooping and how junior staff members were pressured to spy on opposition teams, which was all authorised by their German head coach Eckert, 33.

The commission noted: “It involved far more than innocent activity and a particularly deplorable approach in its use of junior members of staff to conduct the clandestine observations at the direction of senior personnel.

“There was transmission and internal dissemination and analysis of footage and observations. The Commission is not persuaded that this is an exceptional case in which there is evidence that no use was made of the material and therefore no sporting advantage.

“The Commission consider that the evidence demonstrates that the output of the observations fed into analysis conducted by the team, it was discussed with Mr Eckert and others and it was sought so as to inform the strategy for the match. Mr Eckert accepted, as he must, that information such as team selection and injuries is sensitive information which a club would wish to keep private in the build up to a game.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“He also accepted that he had specifically authorised the observations to obtain information about formation (in the Oxford United Incident) and about the availability of a key player (in the Middlesbrough Incident).

“We were unimpressed by suggestions on the part of some of the (Southampton’s) witnesses that they were unaware that these actions were in breach of the Rules. (Southampton) is a member of the EFL and has agreed to be bound by the Rules.”



Sun Sport revealed the shock photo of the moment intern analyst William Salt was caught red-handed recording Boro train less than 48 hours before the first leg of the semi final.

But the report revealed that Salt refused to dress up and disguise himself in an Eastleigh FC kit in an attempt to film Ipswich as he “described the pressure” to the commission that he was placed under.

It added: “The EFL submitted that the evidence supported the view that the observations were authorised at a senior level and that the task was delegated to the intern in relation to the Middlesbrough Incident and the Oxford Incident. He declined to be involved in the Ipswich incident. We heard evidence from the intern who described the pressure he was placed under.

“Such staff were in a vulnerable position without job security and with limited ability to object to or resist the instructions given to them.

“We have concluded that there was, on the part of the respondent (Southampton), a contrived and determined plan from the top down to gain a competitive advantage in competitions of real significance by deliberate attendance at opposition training grounds for the purpose of obtaining tactical and selection information.”



Meanwhile, Southampton captain Taylor Harwood-Bellis has broken his silence on Spygate – and claims he would not have mocked Boro star Aidan Morris with a binoculars celebration had he known the severity of the scandal.

After addressing the squad’s heartbreak, he added: “I’d also like to put on record that, had I known the severity of the situation, I would never have done what I did on the pitch.”

The chaotic events have also led to Southampton players contemplating suing their own club for potential loss of earnings or ripping up their contracts while Eckert now faces the sack for orchestrating, approving and overseeing the spying.

Elsewhere, Hull owner Acun Ilicali considered his own legal action to argue that his side should get automatically promoted without the need to play the final – because Boro have already lost.

Saints legend Matt Le Tissier, though, fumed at the ruling.



He told SunSport: “Personally I try to put a neutral hat on but I feel like the punishment does feel a bit disproportionate.

“It feels like you’ve been put on trial for murder when all you’ve done is stolen a Mars bar from the corner shop.

“You could say it’s a 50-50 chance of whether we go up or not. So I’d probably say it’s like a £100million fine.

“It’s a rule talking about something that gets you literally a microscopic advantage over a team.”

Sports.content:
SOUTHAMPTON captain Taylor Harwood-Bellis has broken his silence on Spygate.

Saints were booted out of the Championship play-offs after being caught spying on semi-final opponents Middlesbrough before the first leg.





Southampton drew 0-0 at the Riverside before a 2-1 win at St Mary’s sent them through to the final – with Harwood-Bellis performing a mocking binoculars celebration at their rivals.

Southampton appealed against the ruling – which also saw a four-point deduction for next season – but this was rejected.

And Harwood-Bellis – who marries Roy Keane’s daughter Leah this summer – took to Instagram on Thursday to share his disappointment.

The defender, accused of mocking Luke Ayling’s stammer during the second leg, wrote: “It’s been nothing but an honour to walk this team out and represent every fan watching in the stands, so it feels right that I speak to you guys directly about what has unfolded this week.

“As players, we are absolutely gutted, disappointed, and heartbroken that it’s come to this.

“As fans, you’ve been unbelievable. Our unbeaten run was driven by your passionate support.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo bursts into tears as footie legend, 41, wins first Al-Nassr trophy after three years in Saudi Arabia
Sports.content:
CRISTIANO RONALDO burst into tears after finally ending his agonising three-year silverware drought with Al-Nassr.

The Portuguese icon was the hero as he fired his side to a 4-1 win over Damac at the Alawwal Park in Riyadh.





The win and the three points confirmed Al-Nassr‘s place as champions of the Saudi Pro League.

Ronaldo, 41, and co headed into the match needing at least a point to hold off rivals Al-Hilal – after seeing the championship slip through their fingers, quite literally, in dramatic scenes against their title rivals last week

That night, Al-Nassr goalkeeper Bento made a catastrophic error in the last seconds of added time to fumble into his own net to hand Al-Hilal a 1-1 draw.

But Ronaldo and Co left nothing to chance this time as the Manchester United legend netted twice in a title-winning rout.

Former Liverpool star Sadio Mane opened the scoring in the 31st minute before Kinsley Coman doubled the lead after the break.

Morlaye Sylla nabbed one back for Damac before Ronaldo stepped up to put the result beyond doubt.



The five-time Ballon d’Or winner netted in the 62nd and 80th minutes to give Al-Nassr a three-goal cushion.

His first goal was the pick of the bunch as he managed to score a rare free-kick from a tight angle.

Despite his explosive goalscoring form since making the mega-money move to the Middle East, team trophies had frustratingly evaded the serial winner.

But after three long years of trying, the legendary attacker can finally call himself a champion once again.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



The triumph means Ronaldo adds yet another domestic crown to his glittering museum, making him a champion in four different top-flight leagues.

He didn’t quite finish the match on the turf, as boss Jorge Jesus subbed him off in the closing stages to receive a standing ovation from adoring fans.

As the final whistle approached, the emotional superstar completely broke down on the bench as the reality of the achievement hit home.

But Ronaldo was soon at the centre of celebrations as he banged a drum for chanting supporters, surrounded by his team-mates.



Next he was flanked by proud partner Georgina Rodriguez and his kids before going up to lift the trophy.

Ronaldo famously made the switch to the Gulf state after a bitter, high-profile fallout with former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag.



He penned a staggering contract worth a mind-blowing £178million-a-year to lead the Saudi football revolution.

And he has certainly kept his side of the bargain on the pitch, defying his advancing years with an incredible goal return.

The goal-machine has plundered 123 goals for Al-Nassr in just 142 games — a mere 18 strikes short of his total United tally.

Astonishingly, he has achieved the breathtaking number in 204 fewer appearances than he made for the Red Devils.



Ronaldo has racked up 28 goals in 30 league games this term, but he will remarkably miss out on the Golden Boot.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

That honour will go to former Brentford striker Ivan Toney, who hit 32 goals in 32 appearances for Al-Ahli, in the process earning himself a surprise spot in England’s World Cup squad.

That will also be the next stop for Ronaldo as he embarks on one final attempt to lead Portugal to football’s ultimate crown.

Sports.title: England star, 25, suffers broken jaw on eve of World Cup squad announcement
Sports.content:
DJED SPENCE has suffered a broken jaw on the eve of England’s World Cup squad announcement.

The Tottenham star suffered the injury in the closing stages of Tuesday’s 2-1 defeat to Chelsea.





Spence, 25, was hurt in a tussle with striker Liam Delap as he took an elbow to the face.

The Blues ace was penalised for the foul, but the full-back is still paying the price.

Spence went for medical checks after the match and it was discovered that he had in fact broken his jaw in the challenge.

The Athletic claim that despite the injury, Spence WILL START for Spurs against Everton on the final day of the Premier League season.

The World Cup hopeful will feature in the match with the help of a protective face mask.

The news of Spence’s mangled mandible comes just a day before Thomas Tuchel‘s squad for this summer‘s World Cup is announced.

Spence has an outside shot of being included in the final 26.

He has only made four appearances for the Three Lions – all of which have come under Tuchel.

The former Nottingham Forest star made history in his debut for England against Serbia in September 2025.

Sports.title: Man Utd transfer news: Rashford's £131m swap suggestion and stance on returning
Sports.content:
Man Utd transfer news: Rashford's £131m swap suggestion and stance on returning

Manchester United star Marcus Rashford has multiple options ahead of the transfer window

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford has spent the season on loan at Barcelona (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Marcus Rashford has been at the centre of transfer speculation throughout the current campaign. The Manchester United forward is on loan at Barcelona and has made no secret of his wish to stay at the Camp Nou.

‌



The 28-year-old, who previously had a stint at Aston Villa, last featured for United in December 2024. Rashford has racked up 14 goals and 14 assists in 48 appearances for Barcelona, playing a key role in Hansi Flick's side clinching La Liga.

‌



The Catalan giants hold the option to sign Rashford permanently for £26million but are yet to activate the clause, with the deadline approaching. As the La Liga champions deliberate over their next move, Mirror Football examines the paths open to Rashford ahead of the summer transfer window.

‌



Real Madrid interest

The Spanish heavyweights are claimed to be eyeing a surprise swoop for Rashford, should Barcelona choose not to exercise their purchase option. Real Madrid are closing in on the appointment of Jose Mourinho as their new manager, who previously worked with the forward during his tenure at Old Trafford.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Spanish outlet Sport has reported that Mourinho is keen for the 28-year-old to link up with him in Madrid. Rashford is regarded as a "valuable addition", with his potential signing also set to "unsettle" Barcelona.

‌



Ruben Amorim set for shock return to management as replacement for another ex-Man Utd boss READ MORE :

Raging Roy Keane rips into Bruno Fernandes and Man Utd stars' behaviour in explosive rant READ MORE :

The move would only be feasible should Barcelona fail to stump up the agreed £26m fee. However, Rashford has already demonstrated his quality in Spanish football and would undoubtedly bolster Real Madrid's ranks.

Man Utd return

Rashford found himself frozen out at Old Trafford during Ruben Amorim's tenure. United's dismissal of the Portuguese manager in January has opened the door for the forward to potentially return to his boyhood club in the summer, should a permanent Barcelona deal fail to come to fruition.

While it appears unlikely, interim boss Michael Carrick stopped short of ruling it out last month. "There's decisions to be made on certain things, and obviously Marcus is in that situation," said Carrick, who played alongside Rashford and later coached him at United.

‌



"But at this point in time, nothing's been decided. It will be because it has to be at a certain point but at this stage, there's nothing to say."

View 3 Images Rashford has previously worked under Michael Carrick (Image: David S. Bustamante/Soccrates/Getty Images)

Barcelona deal

Barcelona have until June 15 to activate their purchase option for Rashford, who has been vocal about his desire to remain beyond this campaign. The Catalan club are yet to reach an agreement with United, as the Reds are unwilling to budge on the £26m asking price, while Barcelona are seeking to renegotiate the fee or arrange a fresh loan agreement.

‌



Mundo Deportivo reports that Rashford has already agreed a three-year contract with Barcelona in principle. However, Barcelona's financial worries could prompt the forward to renegotiate in favour of a five-year deal, enabling the club to spread the transfer fee across a longer timeframe.

The report adds that his Barcelona wages will be 40 per cent lower than his current earnings at Old Trafford. Back in October, when asked whether he wished to stay, Rashford told ESPN: "Oh yeah, for sure. I'm enjoying this football club and I think for anybody who loves football, Barcelona is one of the key clubs in the history of the game. For a player it is an honour."

View 3 Images Rashford has enjoyed his time at Barcelona under Hansi Flick (Image: Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

‌



£131m swap deal

Meanwhile, former United defender Jaap Stam has floated AC Milan as a potential landing spot for Rashford. United have been linked with AC Milan forward Rafael Leao, who carries a £131m release clause, and Stam believes a swap deal could suit both parties.

"Maybe a swap between Rafael Leao and Marcus Rashford could work," Stam told ComeOn. "Leao is also a good player. He has shown his potential at Milan, of course, in what he can do. I think he is a player that should be on the list of targets for Man Utd.

"Having said that, you need to have a look not only at the skill of a player, but also at the mentality of players. You need to consider the situation where the club is, what player they are bringing in that is going to help the club going forward, so that you don't get any irritations from players who are not being picked to start."

Sports.title: Arsenal can trigger £43m release clause to hand Mikel Arteta perfect start to title defence
Sports.content:
Arsenal can trigger £43m release clause to hand Mikel Arteta perfect start to title defence

Arsenal can boost Mikel Arteta's chances of defending the Premier League title next season by signing an exciting player

View 2 Images Arsenal should trigger Victor Valdepenas' release clause (Image: Getty)

Arsenal could secure a dream start to the summer transfer window by snapping up Real Madrid defender Victor Valdepenas. The 19-year-old sensation has a £43million release clause in his contract, and moving swiftly would allow the Gunners to pull off a steal for one of Los Blancos' most promising talents.

‌



Mikel Arteta's first Premier League title triumph has been built on his side's defensive prowess. For all the questions raised about Arsenal's attacking fluidity, there's no disputing the Spaniard's ability to coach defensive tactics, nor his eye for talented defenders.

‌



Cristhian Mosquera's £13m move proved to be one of last summer's bargains, with the former Valencia man clocking up 33 appearances so far in his debut campaign. While Valdepenas' price tag sits closer to the typical expenditure for defensive talents, it would still represent a major coup should Arsenal manage to secure his signature.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The left-back, who can play across the defensive line, came through the Madrid academy and is considered among their finest defensive prospects. He made his senior debut under Xabi Alonso in December against Alaves, marking his only first-team appearance to date. Since then, he has largely remained on the periphery of the senior squad due to his age and has shone for the reserves while helping them claim the UEFA Youth League.

The Gunners are undoubtedly already well aware of his considerable talent, having monitored him extensively throughout this campaign, and Mirror Football understands Valdepenas is a prominent name on their radar ahead of the summer window. While Arteta and sporting director Andrea Berta shortlisted him as a defensive target internally, no formal approach has yet been lodged.

‌



Arsenal missing five stars from training as Max Dowman absence explained READ MORE :

Arsenal set to smash Premier League record with £770m windfall after title win READ MORE :

The teenager is left-footed and, at 6ft 2in, has been labelled a monster and a physical beast by scouts. Combined with his calmness in possession and technical skills, he ticks all the boxes for an Arteta defender.

Valdepenas' ability to operate at left-back, centre-back and left wing-back marks him out as a rare breed of player, reminiscent of Riccardo Calafiori. Arsenal are admittedly already well-served in that area with Piero Hincapie, Calafiori, Jurrien Timber and Myles Lewis-Skelly all capable of playing there.

But the high regard in which Gunners bosses appear to hold him speaks volumes about the youngster's quality. And any chance to bolster the backline heading into next season should not be dismissed, particularly given their injury problems.

‌



View 2 Images The Real Madrid defender has been watched closely by Gunners scouts (Image: Irina R. Hipolito/Europa Press via Getty Images)

Arsenal were even keen on securing Valdepenas in January, soon after Real Madrid had committed him to new terms running until June 2029. Other clubs have since taken notice of this bargain release clause and the Gunners are expected to face competition for his signature this summer.

According to Sky Sport Germany, Eintracht Frankfurt are eager to secure his signature, with the Bundesliga outfit having shown concrete interest. The likes of Bayer Leverkusen and Borussia Dortmund have also been linked with a move.

Article continues below

However, given Arsenal's current standing in European football, the player would likely need little persuasion to opt for north London ahead of a move to Germany.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola 'contact made' as Andy Robertson gives two reasons for struggles
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola 'contact made' as Andy Robertson gives two reasons for struggles

Liverpool's latest news sees the Premier League giants linked with Andoni Iraola while Andy Robertson explains the disappointment of their season

View 3 Images Arne Slot could potentially manage his last Liverpool match on Sunday (Image: Getty)

Liverpool are within touching distance of securing Champions League qualification in their final game of the season. Avoiding defeat against Brentford at Anfield on Sunday will be enough for Arne Slot's side to clinch fifth place.

‌



Even if the Reds were to suffer a fourth league defeat of the campaign against the Bees, Bournemouth would have to reverse a six-goal swing in their final match at Nottingham Forest. Nevertheless, the curtain will finally be drawn on what has been a remarkably disappointing season after this weekend.

‌



The summer could prove to provide more scares for Liverpool fans, with Slot and the hierarchy handed the unenviable task of replacing Mohamed Salah, as well as Andy Robertson, both of whom will leave the club after nine years.

‌



Mirror Football takes a look at the latest reports regarding Andoni Iraola potentially landing at Anfield as well as Robertson's take on what exactly has gone wrong for Liverpool this season.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Conflicting Iraola reports

Reports previously suggested that Arne Slot was likely to continue in his role at Liverpool next season despite the disappointment of the campaign. However, recent claims from Foot Mercato suggest the club's owners, Fenway Sports Group (FSG), are potentially plotting a U-turn on the Dutchman's future.

‌



Liverpool owners told to BAN Mohamed Salah from final day send-off as behaviour addressed READ MORE :

Xabi Alonso refuses to rule out Chelsea selling THREE stars including Enzo Fernandez READ MORE :

They report that Xabi Alonso was considered as a possible replacement for Slot but the former Liverpool midfielder has since joined Chelsea. The French outlet claim Richard Hughes, the Reds' sporting director, is pursuing Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola, who is set to leave the Cherries at the end of the season.

The Spaniard has led Bournemouth to sixth in the Premier League with the club on a remarkable 17-match unbeaten streak - the longest run of any time in the top-flight this season. The 43-year-old will certainly have his list of suitors this summer but Liverpool could have an advantage in the race.

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola will leave Bournemouth at the end of the season (Image: Robin Jones - AFC Bournemouth, AFC Bournemouth via Getty Images)

‌



Hughes was the man who brought Iraola to Bournemouth three years ago during his spell as sporting director at the south coast club as a reunion between the pair could be on the cards. Although the Athletic claim the club's position on Slot remains the same.

Andy Robertson admission

The Liverpool veteran voiced his opinion on what's caused Liverpool's dramatic drop-off when talking to Ian Wright on The Overlap. The 32-year-old discussed the tragic death of Diogo Jota and admitted grieving for their team-mate during their Premier League title defence was "tough."

He told the Arsenal icon: "What happened in the summer with Diogo Jota… nobody could have prepared us for that. The first time I saw my teammates again after the trophy parade was on the way to one of our mate's funeral.

‌



View 3 Images Andy Robertson will bid farewell to Liverpool on Sunday (Image: Getty Images)

"And I don't want to use this as an excuse, but we cannot hide away from this. It's been tough, and we can't hide away from this. Diogo Jota was one of our best mates." Robertson also cited the departure of Trent Alexander-Arnold to Real Madrid as a reason for the Reds' struggles on the pitch.

He explained: "I think obviously we’ve missed him as a player, there’s no doubt about that. We’ve missed him as a character as well. But he’s went on to try something new and sometimes you just have to take your hat off to that."

Sports.title: England star refused to be included in World Cup squad and 'said no' to manager
Sports.content:
Stephen Warnock and Joleon Lescott claim former team-mate Leighton Baines refused to represent England at World Cup 2010. The Everton hero, who retired in 2020, earned 30 caps for his country.

England are gearing up for this year's World Cup in North America, but 16 years ago, the Three Lions endured a tournament that was unforgettable for all the wrong reasons. Fabio Capello's side struggled in the group stage in South Africa before being ousted by Germany in the round of 16 under dubious circumstances.

Former Liverpool defender Warnock was part of the squad as a backup to Ashley Cole, but has admitted he did not think he'd be selected by Capello. The 44-year-old claims that Baines was all set to go but declined as he did not want to be away from his family.

Lescott, who played alongside Baines for Everton and England, concurred, despite the left-back denying it profusely and saying he was simply not picked by Capello, much to his dismay.

‌



You can listen to brand new episodes of In The Mixer on Spotify and Apple Podcasts!

Every 2026 World Cup squad in full as France, Brazil and Portugal submit final lists READ MORE :

ITV heading to New York with Strictly Come Dancing winner to host World Cup - whilst BBC stay in Salford READ MORE :

Speaking on In The Mixer, brought to you by Sky Bet, Warnock said: "I absolutely loved it and a lot of people talk about South Africa and how it was so remote and out of the way. I had a Carlsberg ticket. I was sat in the front row of every game.

"I was sat in the changing room listening to the best players try and work out how to beat a team, watching the players train at the highest level. Who wouldn't want to be there? It was unbelievable.

‌



"The thing was, I didn't think I was going to go. We had two warm-up games. One of them we played Japan. I didn't play in either. Ash [Cole] played in one and Bainsey played in the other.

"I thought, 'I'm not going. That's me done.' Then I got a phone call when he got back…" Lescott interjected, guessing: "Bainsey didn't want to go, did he? He said, 'Nah, that ain't for me.'" Warnock confirmed: "He didn't want to be away from home."

Lescott added: "Bainsey wasn't on that. He didn't like it. He was close to going to Bayern Munich. Like really close. They really wanted him. Desperately wanted Leighton Baines."

View 2 Images Lescott says Baines did not want to move (Image: Getty)

‌



Warnock said: "There was a point before I went to Villa, I was at Blackburn and Bainsey was going to go to Villa and I was going to go to Everton from Blackburn. But Bainesy was just like, 'I don't really fancy it.' He didn't want to move. I mean, a lot of Scousers are like that."

Lescott then revealed Baines was almost part of a historic swap deal: "That's a Scouser thing really. We played Spurs and Harry Redknapp wanted to swap Gareth Bale for Baines.

"Because his record was so bad at the start, but David Moyes said no. It was happening, but Bainsey was also on that too, he was on the Spurs one, [he didn't want to go to] London."

Man Utd news: Dressing room view of Rashford transfer emerges as £110m double deal eyed

Manchester United aim to finish off their 2025/26 Premier League campaign with an away win at Brighton and Hove Albion at the weekend

View 4 Images Marcus Rashford has received the dressing room's thoughts (Image: Ben Roberts Photo/Getty Images)

Manchester United hope to cap off a turbulent season with a crucial away win at Brighton as focus shifts to the summer transfer window. The Red Devils welcomed the return of former club captain Michael Carrick who has steered them to third place in the Premier League.

The current interim boss is set to be rewarded for his recent efforts with a permanent managerial appointment. No official announcement has been made yet but reports suggest this has stalled due to the confirmation of his backroom staff.

Carrick will put pen to paper on a two-year deal with the option of an extra 12 months. His attention will firmly be on the final fixture of the season at the Amex Stadium against Fabian Hürzeler's side.

Plans will already be in place to secure deals for transfer targets this summer, while also allowing some current players to leave for pastures new. Here, Mirror Football has all the latest coming out of Old Trafford.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd bargain transfer gets green light after Spygate scandal as reunion eyed READ MORE :

Dressing room stance on Rashford transfer

Frenkie de Jong believes Marcus Rashford has "earned the right" to become a permanent addition to Barcelona's squad next season. The United forward impressed on loan to the Spanish giants this season, helping them win the La Liga title and the Supercopa .

Rashford made 28 goal contributions in 48 appearances for the league champions and is keen to continue working under Hansi Flick. Now, the thoughts of the Barcelona dressing room have come to light as vice-captain De Jong gives his stamp of approval to the transfer.

View 4 Images Barcelona players want Rashford to stay (Image: Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

The Dutch midfielder told Spanish media outlet Sport: "Yes, he has earned the right to stay. In the minutes he’s played, he’s given us a lot: goals, assists, attacking runs. He’s a fast player who poses a real threat to opposing defences. I’d be delighted if he stays with us.

"I saw him arrive full of enthusiasm. He was very happy to be here, and from the first moment, it was clear he wanted to stay. He’s tried to adapt as best he can, and I’ve seen him doing well."

£110m duo transfer eyed

United have identified Newcastle's Sandro Tonali and Serie A star Ederson as their top two midfield targets this summer. Sky Sports News reports that the club are convinced they will land both players who have a combined valuation of £110million.

4 View 4 Images Sandro Tonali is one of United's top targets (Image: ANDY BUCHANAN / AFP via Getty Images) 4 View 4 Images Ederson is also considered crucial to their plans (Image: Massimo Insabato/Archivio Massimo Insabato/Mondadori Portfolio via Getty Images)

Article continues below

United are said to be fighting with Atletico Madrid over Ederson but have already landed an agreement with the player. A weekly salary of £100,000 is on the table but the club will now hash out a fee with Atalanta - who are demanding £40m.

Reports this week claim the Magpies will likely sell Tonali, but not for less than £70m. Casemiro has already announced his departure after the Brighton game and players like Manuel Ugarte are also said to be eyeing transfers elsewhere.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Eli Junior Kroupi transfer update as target set to wave goodbye to club
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Eli Junior Kroupi transfer update as target set to wave goodbye to club

Arsenal have been linked with Bournemouth's Eli Junior Kroupi ahead of the summer transfer window

View 2 Images Eli Junior Kroupi has enjoyed a successful season with Bournemouth (Image: Robin Jones - AFC Bournemouth/AFC Bournemouth via Getty Images)

Arsenal will have the opportunity to strengthen their squad as reigning Premier League champions in the summer transfer window. Mikel Arteta’s side clinched the title and ended the club’s 22-year wait after Manchester City dropped points on Tuesday night.

‌



It means little will be riding on the Gunners’ upcoming game away at Crystal Palace on Sunday as both teams prepare for European finals next week. Arsenal have a chance to complete a remarkable double and lift the Champions League trophy for the first time in their history against Paris Saint-Germain.

‌



While Arteta is focused on getting the most out of his squad, plans will be formulated over how to improve the team this summer. Bournemouth striker Eli Junior Kroupi has been linked with a move to the Emirates Stadium after his breakthrough season with the Cherries.

‌



Elsewhere, Arsenal are claimed to be interested in Sporting CP’s Morten Hjulmand, who has been tipped to leave the Portuguese giants this summer. Here, Mirror Football looks at some of the biggest stories surrounding the club.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Eli Junior Kroupi update

Arsenal are reportedly interested in Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi but the Bournemouth star is not for sale. The teenager has already earned a place in the Gunners’ hearts by scoring against City on Tuesday, which ultimately gave Arsenal the Premier League title.

‌



Four players who could play their final Arsenal league match against Crystal Palace READ MORE :

PSG boss Luis Enrique gives honest verdict on Arsenal winning the Premier League title READ MORE :

The Daily Mail reports that Arsenal are among the clubs “tracking” the 19-year-old. Chelsea are also claimed to be monitoring Kroupi ahead of the summer window.

However, the report states Bournemouth have insisted that the France U21 international is not for sale. The Cherries have no intention of cashing in on one of their star assets as manager Andoni Iraola prepares to leave the club.

Kroupi has scored 13 in 32 Premier League appearances, averaging a goal every 124 minutes this season. Bournemouth could potentially qualify for the Champions League in their final match against Nottingham Forest on Sunday.

‌



Target prepares for farewell

Sporting CP captain Morten Hjulmand is widely expected to play his last match for the club on Sunday. The Denmark international is preparing to face Torreense in the Taca de Portugal final.

Portuguese outlet Correio da Manha reports that Hjulmand “wants to say goodbye” by lifting the trophy this weekend. The publication has previously described Arsenal as “leading the race” for his signature, alongside Manchester United.

View 2 Images Morten Hjulmand has been tipped to leave Sporting in the summer (Image: Maciej Rogowski/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images)

‌



The defensive midfielder’s contract includes a £69million release clause but he is expected to leave for around half of that amount, with Sporting already working on finding his replacement. Atletico Madrid and Manchester City are also claimed to be interested in the 26-year-old.

Hjulmand joined Sporting from Lecce in 2023, becoming captain the following year. The Dane has won two Primeira Liga titles and one Taca de Portugal during his time at the club as he looks to add another major honour to his collection.

Sports.title: Koepka makes storming eight-under start as Scheffler lurks in Texas
Sports.content:
Brooks Koepka fired a storming eight-under 63 to take the clubhouse lead in the first round of the The CJ Cup Byron Nelson in Texas.

Four days on from the conclusion of the PGA Championship, won by Englishman Aaron Rai, regular tour action in the US resumed at TPC Craig Ranch with world No 1 and defending tournament champion Scottie Scheffler headlining the field.

But it was former No 1 and five-time major winner Koepka, playing in a group alongside Scheffler, who made the most eye-catching start in McKinney on his 11th appearance back on the PGA Tour thanks to a bogey-free opening round featuring six birdies and one eagle.

Starting from the 10th hole, Koepka birdied the par-four 11th before finding an eagle at the next hole, the par-five 12th. After a further birdie at the 14th helped him go out in a four-under 31, the American birdied the second, fourth, fifth and sixth on his way in for a round of 63.

Koepka has returned to the PGA Tour this year after four seasons on LIV Golf and has so far recorded a best finish of tied-ninth at the Cognizant Classic in February. He finished tied 55th last week at Aronimink after sliding out of contention on the final day with a 74.

"Finally, I felt good with the putter," said Koepka.

"I felt good the last few days with it when I was working in my studio. Then when I got here, it felt very comfortable.

"Just happy with the way everything went today."

As it stands with Thursday's play continuing, Koepka leads by one shot from a group of five players - Argentina's Emiliano Grillo, South Korea's Si Woo Kim, Germany's Stephan Jaeger and American duo Keith Mitchell and Michael Thorbjornsen - tied on seven under.

Texan resident Scheffler, who won last year's tournament on 31 under par to equal the record or the fewest amount of strokes in a PGA Tour event, opened his title defence with a five-under 66.

In the group with Koepka and Kim, starting at the 10th, Scheffler birdied the 12th and 13th before finishing his day by going three under through his final five holes, including a round-ending birdie.

"I felt like I was getting lapped out there for a little bit," said Scheffler.

"So I was fortunate to make a couple birdies late in the round and keep myself in the tournament.

"I feel like sometimes in these tests, once you start getting behind, you can start falling pretty far behind, and it can be difficult to catch up. It was nice to stay in it.

"Overall, it was a fun group. We had good momentum in the group the whole day. Brooks played great, and Si Woo played really nice as well. Hopefully more of that the next couple days."

Sports.title: Russell insists relationship with Wolff rock solid amid 'external noise'
Sports.content:
George Russell insists his relationship with his Mercedes boss Toto Wolff remains rock solid and that he treats speculation over his future with the team as "just external noise".

Russell is under pressure going into this weekend's Canadian Grand Prix having surprisingly fallen 20 points behind his team-mate Kimi Antonelli at the top of the Drivers' Championship after three successive victories for the Italian teenager.

With Mercedes having the strongest performing car at the start of the new Formula 1 regulations implemented for this season, Russell had been considered a clear favourite for the title given the significant edge in experience the 28-year-old holds over Antonelli.

Despite Russell's consistently impressive performances since joining Mercedes as Lewis Hamilton's team-mate in 2022, there has been intermittent speculation over his future with the team over the last couple of years amid Wolff's interest in signing four-time world champion Max Verstappen from Red Bull.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff was seen chatting with Jos Verstappen in the paddock as speculation continues over son Max's future at Red Bull.

Asked by Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle on Thursday whether his relationship with Wolff remains "rock solid", Russell replied: "Yeah, for sure.

"I mean, firstly, I don't read any of that (speculation) because even the positive press doesn't really bring anything. I just focus on myself."

Russell comments came around the same time Wolff was seen having a lengthy conversation with Verstappen's father Jos outside of Mercedes' hospitality unit in the Montreal paddock.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Brundle praised 'impressive' Kimi Antonelli but believes he will have to put on a big performance to stop Mercedes teammate George Russell in Canada.

"We have a super close relationship," Russell continued. "We've been through the tough moments in the last four years trying to bring Mercedes back on top, and now we're in this position that we're both in a fortunate place, that we're fighting for wins week in, week out.

"So, yes, all of that for me is just external noise."

'Toto is very different to other team bosses'

Russell got his Mercedes seat just after the team had sealed an eighth successive constructors' title, but the Brit has had far less opportunities for victories than most anticipated his jump from Williams would bring, with Red Bull and McLaren dominating under the previous set of regulations.

Throughout his time as Mercedes chief, Wolff has shown his willingness to let his drivers battle for titles, most notably when Hamilton and Nico Rosberg fiercely duelled over several seasons.

Asked by Brundle whether Wolff was different to team principals who might only be able to "love one driver at a time", Russell said: "Toto is very different to a lot of team bosses in Formula 1.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Toto Wolff says George Russell will never stop fighting and that the 20-point gap from teammate Kimi Antonelli won't deter him.

"I think you saw it with Lewis and Nico that he's always given that equal opportunity to both.

"Even when it was Lewis and I, and Kimi and I last year, Mercedes have never been a team to bring an update just to one driver, they always bring it together.

"And he's made it clear that there's equal opportunity. So, it's down to us to sort the rest, as it should be."

Antonelli trying to 'avoid as many distractions as possible'

Having gone from title outsider to favourite after claiming the first three victories of his career in succession, Antonelli says he is trying to avoid the potential distractions that come with his raised profile.

"Social media I don't look at all during the race week. I try to avoid as many distractions as possible," the 19-year-old said on Thursday.

"All I want is just to try and be as focused as possible on the goal of the weekend, so focusing on the process, on what I have to do.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Having won the last three races, Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli is confident he can maintain his recent good form as he looks to win a maiden world championship.

"I know expectations are very high now, especially after this strong start of the year.

"But I try not to worry too much about it and not get carried away from it. I just try to, as I did all the other weekends, just try to focus on what I have to do and, also, enjoying as well the weekend, enjoying the driving.

"I know if I do these things well, which is also staying present in every moment, that a good result will come."

Sports.title: Verstappen suggests proposed 2027 rule changes could convince him to stay in F1
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen has suggested tweaks to the 2027 Formula 1 regulations could convince him to remain in the sport.

Verstappen revealed at the end of March he was considering walking away from F1 at the end of this season due to frustrations about the new 2026 power unit rules which forced the drivers to drive in an unnatural way to optimise lap time.

The FIA tweaked the regulations for the last race in Miami but agreed with the teams during the break ahead of this weekend's Canadian Grand Prix to increase the proportion of total power coming from the internal combustion engine and decrease the electrical output.

The power split would become closer to 60-40 under the 2027 changes in a reduction of the electrical power element, thus leading to a return to last year's driving style.

Once power unit manufacturers have voted on the final agreed package, the measures will go to World Motor Sport Council to be rubber-stamped, a regulatory process which is likely to be a formality at that stage.

"It's definitely heading into a very positive direction. I think it's the minimum I was hoping for. I think it's really nice that's what they want to do. That's definitely what I think also the sport needs," said Verstappen, who has a Red Bull contract until the end of 2028.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen sarcastically waves at Pierre Gasly after being overtaken by the Alpine at the Japanese Grand Prix.

Asked if it will boost his chances of staying in F1 next year, he added: "Yeah, definitely. I just want a good product in Formula 1, and that will for sure improve the product.

"What I said before with the changes, hopefully that will happen next year, that will already help a lot. I've always said it doesn't matter if I had a good car or not, it's just a product, and I think the product will improve like that, so naturally I think then the enjoyment will go up as well."

Verstappen was the most vocal critic of the current power unit regulations but most of the grid have expressed concerns about not being able to push to the limit, particularly in qualifying.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking ahead of the Canadian Grand Prix, Max Verstappen reflected on his experience at the Nurburgring 24 Hours endurance race

But Verstappen says the FIA has listened to the drivers, which has been one of the most positive aspects of the rules discussions this year.

The Red Bull driver said: "The more you achieve in the sport, I think, actually, you have maybe have a bit more of a voice. In the beginning of the year, I had a few meetings with F1, and then, of course, with other drivers, with the FIA as well, and it's just great that they open-minded and they listen to the drivers.

"I think we speak, or at least most of us speak, in the interest of the sport, and we just want to make it a better product, and that's why you come up with the recommendations, and I think what they are trying to do is definitely the right thing."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Brundle believes the Canadian Grand Prix could deliver drama this year, as the new F1 cars face the challenges of the circuit’s demanding layout

Norris, Antonelli agree with F1 direction for 2027

Reigning world champion Lando Norris has also been concerned about the regulations this year. At the third round in Japan he did not want to overtake the driver in front due to complexities around the power unit system which meant not overtaking would be a potential benefit.

"I certainly think that's a great direction. We all welcome that as drivers. We all want that," he said regarding the agreement to change the 2027 engine design.

"I think that will eliminate a lot of the talks that we have about not going on throttle here and doing this and that.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris has urged McLaren to keep pushing as they look to overhaul Mercedes at the front of the grid

"Maybe it's not the perfect world that we all want. But it certainly will be in the correct direction, I would say. That's what we want for the future. It's what we want for racing. It's what all of us want as drivers.

"The FIA are doing as much as they can. You still have to try and please a lot of people. But if you want the sport to be better. If you want the racing to be better. If you want the drivers to be better and happier, that's certainly the correct direction to go."

Mercedes have won all four races so far this season and have extracted the most from the new power unit regulations, with Kimi Antonelli leading the Drivers' Championship.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Having won the last three races, Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli is confident he can maintain his recent good form as he looks to win a maiden World Championship

Even though Mercedes have the fastest car with the current rules, Antonelli is still happy the rules are set to change next year.

"I definitely cannot complain about the PU and everything. But for sure, at the end of the day, we all want the sport to go in the right direction. We all want the best for the sport," said the Italian.

"There's a lot of talking with the FIA, with all the teams. Everyone seems to be very open, ourselves included, to make changes to improve the sport, so for sure let's see what's going to happen, if the change is going to be official.

"It's going to be more similar to what it was last year, so let's see. Definitely in terms of from a driving point of view, it will be much more natural."
